subject.title: gh-issues skill: untrusted issue body injected directly into sub-agent prompt

question: Should OpenClaw require runtime untrusted-content handling for gh-issues plus accepted per-spawn child tool scoping before considering this issue fixed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the permanent fix defines a security/API boundary across skill prompt construction, sessions_spawn tool policy, durable child-session state, and SECURITY.md hardening-versus-vulnerability semantics.

options.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
options.body: Land or replace the per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent isolation before closing this issue.

options.title: Accept prompt-only hardening
options.body: Treat prompt guidance and global subagent policy as sufficient defense in depth while documenting that hostile issue bodies remain within the operator-granted agent trust boundary.

options.title: Defer unified delegation policy
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers design one delegated-agent content and capability policy for skills, hooks, cron, and sessions_spawn.

recommendation.title: Require runtime boundary and toolsAllow
recommendation.body: Land or replace the per-spawn tool-scoping work and add gh-issues content wrapping, summarization, length bounding, or equivalent isolation before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across sessions_spawn introduction, sandbox require mode, and the current security/API boundary.
